Grow & score: Select a seedling. Count the trichomes on the right margin and use Record my count. Hand-count at least five plants before using Auto-count the rest, unless your teacher gives other instructions.
Open Data to review the scores and Graph to inspect the histogram. Record the generation 1 mean, spread, and distribution shape; answer the questions below the simulation.
Select & pollinate: Write your prediction before selecting parents. Choose the selection direction and fraction, then use Mark selected plants. Generation 1 must be scored first.
Compare the selected-parent mean with the generation 1 mean. Press Pollinate and wait for completion, then Harvest seed and plant generation 2. Explain your selection in the response box.
Generation 2: Press Score generation 2. Compare the generations using Graph and Data; record the means and spread.

Calculate the selection differential S, response R, and heritability estimate h² using the formulas on the page. Enter your calculations and use Check my numbers. If assigned, use Select again to investigate additional generations.
Design: Write a testable question, hypothesis, variables, and controls before running the experiment. Choose the trait, selection direction, and number of generations.
Run experiment and compare the resulting generations in Graph and Data. Record the settings and results; explain the pattern and use the available statistics to support your conclusion.

Card model: Write your prediction, then Mate one generation. Use Run 5 generations and inspect how allele frequencies change.
Choose another case and repeat. Record the case, settings, and allele frequencies, then compare the cases in the response box.
Build the model: Write your prediction and examine the spreadsheet model. Recalculate at least three times and Record this run after each recalculation with 16 zygotes.
Change the number of zygotes to 100, then 1000; record runs at each size. Compare sampling variation and answer the questions below the model.
Many generations: Predict what will happen, then Run model with drift only. Compare populations of N = 10, 100, and 1000, using Record result for each run.

Turn on one additional force such as selection, mutation, or migration and run again. Record the starting conditions and final allele frequencies; answer the questions and complete the chi-square practice if assigned.
Design: Write your question and hypothesis. Choose one independent variable and its levels; keep other settings constant.
Run experiment and use the chart and Data table to compare outcomes. Describe the variation, results, and whether the evidence supports your hypothesis.

Morphology: Read the organism evidence cards and complete the trait table. Use Check my table, then revisit the evidence for any highlighted entries.
Select organisms sharing a trait and use Group selected organisms to build clades. Inspect the resulting tree, choose a fossil placement hypothesis, and explain the evidence for your placement.
BLAST the genes: Write your prediction. Select fossil gene A, press BLAST, and open at least two alignments to inspect the matches.
Use Record top 5 hits. Repeat for genes B and C. Record organism names, percent identities, scores, and E-values from your own results. A distance tree is available under More options if assigned.
Place the fossil: Compare the recorded molecular results with your morphology hypothesis. Use the placement controls on this page to place the fossil on the tree.
Explain your final placement using evidence from multiple genes and the morphology comparison. Discuss any limits or disagreement between the evidence sources.
Design: Write a molecular-clock question, hypothesis, and variables. Choose a query organism, a gene, and the organisms to search, then BLAST your query and Add all hits to clock table.
Repeat for other genes only as needed for your question. In Graph, examine percent identity versus divergence time. Record the gene, cutoff, number of fitted points, slope, intercept, and R².
Use the displayed cutoff when checking a regression; points outside it are shown but do not contribute to the fit. Keep genes separate. Describe the pattern, limitations, and conclusion.

SA:V: Test the indicator by adding HCl and NaOH to the separate tubes. Record your observations and write a diffusion prediction.
Choose three blocks and a soak time, then Soak, cut, and measure. In Data, calculate surface area, volume, SA:V, and percent diffused for every block.
Use Check my calculations, revise flagged entries, inspect Graph, and answer the questions below.
Model cells: Predict the effects of the bag contents. Use Weigh, soak 30 min, re-weigh to collect measurements for all five bags.
Run the set at least twice for replicates. Calculate percent mass change for each bag in Data, use Check my % changes, and compare the graph before answering the questions.
Plasmolysis: Write your prediction. Choose a solution, then Add solution under cover slip. Focus the microscope and observe the cells during the simulated treatment.
Use Record this view, count plasmolyzed cells, and enter the count in Data. Test at least three solutions. If assigned, rinse with distilled water and record whether the appearance changes.
Water potential: Identify all six cups using the information and controls on the page. Select a tissue and run Weigh, soak overnight, re-weigh.
Run each assigned tissue twice for replicates. Calculate the mass changes and use the graph to estimate the isotonic concentration.
Use the page's temperature, units, and water-potential formulas to calculate ψS and tissue ψ. Enter your values and Check my calculation; explain your evidence.
Design: Write your question, hypothesis, variables, and control. Choose the independent variable and enter valid levels.
Run experiment, compare Graph and Data, and describe your results and whether they support the hypothesis.

Sink disks: Set up the bicarbonate and water-control cups as shown. Add the indicated drop of soap to wet the leaf surfaces.
Pull vacuum, release, and repeat until the disks sink. Use Pour to place the prepared disks into the two cups. Complete this preparation before starting Float assay.
Float assay: Write your prediction and confirm the disks have been sunk and poured. Set the assay conditions and Start timer; follow the automatically recorded floating counts in Data.
Run long enough to evaluate whether half the disks float, up to the available observation limit. Record the number of disks, conditions, duration, and counts for each cup.

Calculate ET₅₀ and 1/ET₅₀ from your own counts and check them using the page controls. If half never float, report that ET₅₀ exceeds the observation time; do not invent a measured ET₅₀ or zero rate. Answer the procedure questions.
Design: Write your question and hypothesis. Choose one variable and valid levels, keep other conditions constant, and include controls and replicate cups.
Use Run all cups. Compare the recorded counts, ET₅₀ results, and Graph. Treat cups that never reach half floating as censored observations, then explain your findings and limitations.

Microrespirometer: Write your prediction. Keep equilibration and the insulated bath enabled for the first comparison; record your organism, temperature, and other settings.
Start 25-min run. In Data, calculate the change during each interval and the corrected seeds-minus-beads values in the editable columns. Use Check my calculations.
Open Graph and determine the oxygen-uptake rate from the fitted slope. Enter the rate with units and check it. Repeat for three runs if your teacher assigns the mean and SE comparison.
Gas sensors: Write your prediction and choose the sensor and chamber contents. Press Collect data and review the resulting graph and table.
Repeat with all three sensors. If assigned, compare germinating peas with glass beads and KOH on versus off. Record the sensor, units, conditions, and observed direction and rate of change.
Design: Write the proposal, including a question, hypothesis, variable, control, and constants. Choose the organism and conditions, using at least three replicate respirometers per run.

Run trial(s), change only your independent variable, and collect the comparison groups. Group the graph by that variable and report rates with units, variability, one sample calculation, and a conclusion.

Mitosis model: Use the main stage button to replicate DNA and continue through mitosis. At metaphase, drag chromosomes to the plate; then move sister chromatids to opposite poles. The alternative alignment and pulling buttons can assist with dragging.
Complete every chromosome/DNA entry in Data and Check my table. Put the stained-cell cards in order and Check order. Explain what changes between stages.
Root tips: Write your prediction. Choose a jar and root tip, make the slide, and focus the microscope. Classify every whole cell using I, P, M, A, or T.
Record counts for this tip, then choose a different tip. Repeat for three tips in each jar. Do not record the same tip as another replicate.
Add class data if assigned. Calculate mitotic indices and use the chi-square tool with the expected values requested on the page. Record the statistic, degrees of freedom, and conclusion.
Cancer karyotypes: Write your hypothesis before examining the chromosomes. Inspect normal, HeLa, and CML cells, counting each chromosome once; use Karyotype if assigned.
Enter counts for all three cells in Data, use Check my counts, and recount flagged cells. Answer the HeLa and Philadelphia chromosome questions using the observed evidence.
Meiosis model: Write your prediction and use Next stage through meiosis I and II. Watch the homologs and sister chromatids separately.
Use Record these gametes when the four gametes appear. If assigned, change the crossover, orientation, or nondisjunction condition and record another run.
Run 200 meioses, inspect the gamete distribution in Graph and Data, and complete the requested comparisons and chi-square analysis.
Sordaria: Predict the outcome, focus the field, and score mature asci as 4:4 or crossover. Do not score immature or incomplete asci.
Record this field. Use New squash / next field and repeat until at least 50 asci have been recorded.
Calculate percent crossover and map units using the formulas on the page, check your calculations, and add class data if assigned. Explain sampling variation and your comparison.
Design: Write your question and hypothesis. Choose a factor and at least two levels including the control; use at least three root tips per level.
Grow, fix, and score roots. Compare mitotic indices in Graph and Data and explain the pattern, variability, and conclusion.

Transform: Follow Do this step through the displayed protocol. Keep track of the +pGLO and −pGLO tubes and record the settings for every step.

Add transformation solution; chill the tubes; add cells; add plasmid only to the designated tube; incubate on ice; heat shock; return to ice; add LB and recover; then spread the cells on the plates. Use the times, volumes, and temperatures shown on the page or assigned by your teacher.
Before incubation, enter predictions for all six plates. Incubate plates, then compare room-light and UV views. Record growth and fluorescence separately.

Select the +pGLO LB/amp plate and click each colony to count it. Calculate total DNA, fraction plated, DNA spread, and transformation efficiency using the displayed amounts. Check the calculation, then Add this run.
For another transformation, use the page's new-run/reset control and confirm your completed run remains in saved history before proceeding.
Design: Write a testable question, hypothesis, variables, and controls. Choose one variable and its levels, with at least three transformations per level.

Run experiment and compare efficiencies and variation in Graph and Data. If assigned, choose a large or satellite colony, select a fresh plate, and Streak and incubate; test both colony types and compare UV observations.

Restriction enzymes: Inspect the template strand and predict the number of fragments before digesting it. Choose the enzyme, run the digest, and compare fragment ends and sizes.
Use the λ restriction map to test enzyme combinations. Record the selected enzymes, cut sites, and fragment lengths; check that lengths sum to the starting molecule's length.
Run a gel: Select a sample tube and an empty well to load it. Repeat for the required samples, including the HindIII marker and uncut λ control; record the lane order and loading conditions.
Connect the leads as shown, set the gel percentage and voltage, and Power on. Watch the dye front; stop with about 1 cm remaining before the end of the gel.
Stain, then destain the gel. Wait for each stage or use Skip ahead. Record observations of the visible bands before measuring.
Standard curve: Measure each visible band or use Measure all visible bands for each lane. For the marker lane, enter the supplied known sizes in the correct band order; use the reference on the page rather than calculating the known sizes.
Keep the >20,000-bp doublet exclusion enabled for the standard fit unless your teacher directs otherwise. Check log₁₀(bp) versus distance, its equation, and R².

Read unknown-band estimates from this fit. Label estimates beyond the fitted marker-distance range as extrapolations; discuss why they are unreliable. Repeat measurements or gels if assigned and report uncertainty.
Design: crime scene: Enter the case number assigned by your teacher; do not assume the personal default is the assigned case. Write your question, prediction, and plan.
Load the marker, blood, and suspect samples. Run, stop, stain, destain, and measure the gel using the same procedure as the practice gel; enter known marker sizes.

Choose and justify a matching tolerance based on measurement variation. Compare corresponding fragment estimates, including missing or extra bands, and state which profiles are consistent with the evidence and what the evidence cannot establish.

Part 1: NPP: Write your diagram prediction. Advance the plants to at least day 7, then Harvest to blot and weigh the first set. Use Dry 48 h to obtain dry masses.
Advance to about day 14 or later and harvest and dry another set. In Data, calculate the requested percent biomass, stored energy, and NPP summary values using the supplied conversion factor.
Measure dark respiration with Seal 5 plants on the same day as a harvest. Complete the NPP, respiration, and GPP calculations and answer the questions about dry mass and uncertainty.
Part 2: Larvae: Predict the energy flow in the larva diagram. Use Day 0: weigh, then feed to run the three-day barn experiment.
Run at least three barns for replicate data. Record food, larvae, frass, and control measurements in Data.

Work through the energy audit for barn 1 using the supplied energy conversion factors. Apply the evaporation correction as requested and calculate consumption, growth, frass, respiration, and efficiencies. Answer the comparison questions.
Design: Write your question and hypothesis. Select an organism, one independent variable, and at least two levels including the standard condition; describe controls and constants.
Run experiment and compare Graph and Data. Record your settings, replicate results, and units, then explain the energy pattern and uncertainty.

Leaf area: Count full grid squares and squares crossed by the leaf edge. Enter both counts and Calculate and record.
Use Trace a different leaf, count again, and record at least three leaves. Review the areas and answer the questions about your measurement method.
Stomata: Write your prediction. Choose the species and leaf surface, use 400X, and adjust fine focus until the guard cells are clear. Click each stoma to tally it.
Record this field once. Use Move to a new field before counting and recording another replicate; repeated Record clicks do not create independent observations.

Record at least three fields for the same slide and surface at 400X. Calculate stomatal density from the mean count and field area, use Check, then compare surfaces/species as assigned and answer the questions.
Water loss: Write your prediction and record the plant, method, conditions, and replicate count. Run the control first, then a treatment with the same plant and method.
In Data, calculate rate ÷ leaf area for every plant using the unit scale shown, then Check my rate/area values.
Compare the time graph and adjusted-rate summaries. Keep method-specific units distinct and explain how the treatment compares with its control.
Design: Write your question, hypothesis, variables, and constants. Change one factor and include a default-condition control.
Run replicates for at least two groups. Choose Group A and B for the t-test when each has sufficient replicate data. Report rates, units, variability, and the conclusion supported by your comparison.

Pre-lab: Read the reference card and focus the sexing microscope. Identify a fly as Female or Male, then Next fly; identify at least five, aiming for four correct identifications.
Complete the pre-lab quiz and the question about where you see fruit flies. If assigned, Play demo and compare the taxis/kinesis panels.
Geotaxis vial: Write your prediction. Set the number and age of flies, then Tap down and watch 30 s.
Run at least three trials, comparing young and old flies as assigned. Record counts and timing from Data and answer the three questions below.
Choice chamber: Write your preference predictions. Run a distilled-water versus distilled-water control first; keep track of End A and End B.
Test four substances against water, completing each trial and recording interval/final counts as prompted. Stopping mid-run does not record a completed trial.
Use Swap ends and repeat if assigned to investigate position effects. Examine χ² and the decision for each completed trial in Data; explain the result using your actual counts.
Design: Write your question and hypothesis and identify variables, controls, and constants. Choose the stimuli and other settings for a control and treatment comparison.
Run trials for at least two conditions that differ only in the independent variable. Compare the graphs and counts and explain preference, variability, and possible position effects.

Procedure 1: Write your enzyme-versus-control prediction. Review the tube recipes and choose palette or spectrophotometer measurement before starting the trial.

Combine tubes & start timer. In palette mode, compare each recorded tube image with the palette and enter colors for enzyme and control at every time in Data. In spectrophotometer mode, review the recorded absorbances instead.
Use Graph to compare initial slopes and Data to check time points. Select a baseline time for later assays and explain your choice and constants. Repeat the trial if assigned.

Keep units tied to the method: palette levels/min and absorbance change/min are different measures. Small negative blank-corrected absorbances can reflect noise near zero; an endpoint reading ratio is not a rate ratio.
Procedure 2: pH: Complete Procedure 1 first so you can choose a baseline time. Predict the pH response, select buffers, and keep other recipe components and reading times constant.
Use Combine all pairs & start. Run at least three trials. Enter each palette reading in Data if using the color method; otherwise review the absorbance-change readings.
Compare the graph, identify the greatest measured response from your own data, and describe the pH pattern and variation.
Design: Write your question, hypothesis, variables, controls, and constants. Choose one variable and at least two valid levels with a comparison/control condition.
Run experiment and compare Graph and Data. Use comparable time intervals and the same measurement method to calculate rates; report the pattern, variability, and evidence supporting your conclusion.
